questions.question: Silver-Meal (demand $D_j$, setup $K_i$, holding $h_k$ per unit carried from period $k$ to $k+1$) covers periods $i,\dots,t$ by one order in period $i$, with $TC(i,t)=K_i+\sum_{j=i+1}^tD_j\sum_{k=i}^{j-1}h_k$ and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$. Over what is the cost averaged in $TCU(i,t)$?
options: The $t-i+1$ periods covered by the order
The $\sum_{j=i}^tD_j$ units in the order
All $n$ periods of the planning horizon
The covered periods with positive demand

questions.question: Silver-Meal (demand $D_j$, setup $K_i$, holding $h_k$ per unit carried from period $k$ to $k+1$) covers periods $i,\dots,t$ by one order in period $i$, with $TC(i,t)=K_i+\sum_{j=i+1}^tD_j\sum_{k=i}^{j-1}h_k$ and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$. With a constant holding cost $h_k=h$, how much holding cost does the demand $D_j$ of a covered period $j>i$ add to $TC(i,t)$?

The Silver-Meal heuristic orders in period $i$ for periods $i,\dots,t$, with $TC(i,t)$ the setup plus holding cost and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$; it extends $t$ while $TCU$ decreases and stops at the first local minimum. Why can this stopping rule miss a cheaper plan?
options: $TCU(i,t)$ is convex in $t$, so the first minimum is global
Coverages beyond the first rise are infeasible for the order
It always finds the optimum, as the exact method also stops there
It checks just the next average, not later ordering patterns

questions.question: Silver-Meal (demand $D_j$, setup $K_i$, holding $h_k$ per unit carried from period $k$ to $k+1$) covers periods $i,\dots,t$ by one order in period $i$, with $TC(i,t)=K_i+\sum_{j=i+1}^tD_j\sum_{k=i}^{j-1}h_k$ and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$. The unit purchase price is the same in every period. Why does the heuristic leave purchasing cost out of $TC(i,t)$?
options: Purchasing cost is already part of the setup cost $K_i$
Every plan buys all demand at that price, a fixed total
Purchasing cost is zero in the dynamic lot-size model
Including it would always make one single order the best plan

questions.question: For a dynamic lot-size problem in which the lowest total cost is sought, the Silver-Meal heuristic returns a feasible ordering plan with cost $C_{\mathrm{SM}}$, while the optimal cost is $C^*$. Which relation always holds?
options: $C^*\ge C_{\mathrm{SM}}$, so the heuristic gives a lower bound
$C^*=C_{\mathrm{SM}}$, since Silver-Meal solves it exactly
$C^*\le C_{\mathrm{SM}}$, the heuristic gives an upper bound
No relation, as a heuristic plan may be infeasible

questions.question: An order in period 1 covers periods 1 to 3 with demands $D=(20,30,10)$, setup cost $K_1=50$ and holding cost $h=1$ per unit per period carried. With $TC(1,3)=K_1+\sum_{j=2}^3D_j(j-1)h$, what is the average cost per covered period $TCU(1,3)=\frac{TC(1,3)}{3}$?

The Silver-Meal heuristic orders in period $i$ for periods $i,\dots,t$, with $TC(i,t)$ the setup plus holding cost and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$; it extends $t$ while $TCU$ decreases and stops at the first local minimum. Starting at $i=1$, the averages are $TCU(1,1)=60$, $TCU(1,2)=45$, $TCU(1,3)=47$, $TCU(1,4)=40$. Which periods does the first order cover?
options: Periods 1 to 4
Period 1 alone
Periods 1 to 3
Periods 1 to 2

questions.question: The Silver-Meal heuristic orders in period $i$ for periods $i,\dots,t$, with $TC(i,t)$ the setup plus holding cost and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$; it extends $t$ while $TCU$ decreases and stops at the first local minimum. Demands are $D=(15,25,10,30)$ and the first order, placed in period 1, covers periods 1 to 3. How many units does it order?

One order in period 1 covers periods 1 to 3 with demands $D=(10,20,5)$ and setup cost $K_1=40$. Holding costs $h_1=1$, $h_2=3$, $h_3=2$ are charged per unit carried from period $k$ to $k+1$, and $TC(1,3)=K_1+\sum_{j=2}^3D_j\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}h_k$. What is $TC(1,3)$?

A Silver-Meal plan for a dynamic lot-size problem has setup plus holding cost 90. The 60 units of total demand are bought at a common unit price of 4. What total cost including purchasing should be reported?

Silver-Meal (demand $D_j$, setup $K_i$, holding $h_k$ per unit carried from period $k$ to $k+1$) covers periods $i,\dots,t$ by one order in period $i$, with $TC(i,t)=K_i+\sum_{j=i+1}^tD_j\sum_{k=i}^{j-1}h_k$ and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$. Covering one more period $t+1$ adds the holding cost $A=D_{t+1}\sum_{k=i}^{t}h_k$ to $TC$. When does the average fall, $TCU(i,t+1)<TCU(i,t)$?
options: When $A<K_i$, the setup cost of the order
When $A<TCU(i,t)$, the current average cost
When $TC(i,t+1)<TC(i,t)$, the total falls
When $D_{t+1}$ is below the average covered demand

questions.question: The Silver-Meal heuristic orders in period $i$ for periods $i,\dots,t$, with $TC(i,t)$ the setup plus holding cost and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$; it extends $t$ while $TCU$ decreases and stops at the first local minimum. With demands and holding costs fixed, the setup cost $K$ (equal in all periods) is raised. How does the number of periods covered by the first order change?
options: It becomes shorter, since each order now costs more
It stays the same, since $K$ cancels from the averages
It grows in proportion to the increase in $K$
It stays the same or grows, as $K$ raises each average

questions.question: The Silver-Meal heuristic orders in period $i$ for periods $i,\dots,t$, with $TC(i,t)$ the setup plus holding cost and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$; it extends $t$ while $TCU$ decreases and stops at the first local minimum. Starting at period $i$, $TCU(i,t)$ is still decreasing when $t$ reaches the last period $n$ of the horizon. What does the heuristic do?
options: Covers through $n$, as no later average exists
Stops at $n-1$, as a minimum needs a later rise
Extends past $n$ with periods of zero demand
Restarts at $n$ with a separate final order

questions.question: Four periods have demands $D=(20,30,10,40)$, setup cost $K=60$ per order and holding cost 1 per unit per period carried. Silver-Meal extends each order while the average cost per covered period (setup plus holding) decreases, then restarts. Which order plan results?

Three periods each have demand 10, setup cost is 30 per order and holding cost 1 per unit per period carried. Silver-Meal extends an order only while the average cost per covered period strictly decreases (on a flat tie it stops at the first minimum), then restarts. Which order plan results?

Apply Silver-Meal (extend an order while its setup-plus-holding cost per covered period decreases, then restart) to demands $D=(40,0,10)$, with a setup cost of 50 for each order and a holding cost of 1 per unit for each period carried. Which order plan results?

Silver-Meal (demand $D_j$, setup $K_i$, holding $h_k$ per unit carried from period $k$ to $k+1$) covers periods $i,\dots,t$ by one order in period $i$, with $TC(i,t)=K_i+\sum_{j=i+1}^tD_j\sum_{k=i}^{j-1}h_k$ and $TCU(i,t)=\frac{TC(i,t)}{t-i+1}$. Why does the heuristic compare the averages $TCU(i,t)$ rather than the totals $TC(i,t)$?
options: $TC$ rises or stays level as $t$ grows, so totals stop at $t=i$
Totals would always favour covering the whole horizon at once
Averages and totals choose the same $t$, so the choice is cosmetic
Averages give the exact optimum, while totals only approximate it

questions.question: In a dynamic lot-size problem with the same setup cost $K$ in every period and positive demand in each of the $n$ periods, Silver-Meal chooses each cover where its average cost per covered period is a first local minimum, starting from $TCU(i,i)=K$. Compared with ordering every period (cost $nK$), what must hold?
options: Silver-Meal can cost more than $nK$, as it ignores later periods
Silver-Meal always attains the optimum, which is below $nK$
Silver-Meal costs at most $nK$, since each average is at most $K$
Both plans always cost exactly $nK$ in such instances

questions.question: Demands are $D=(10,40,20)$, setup cost 50 per order and holding cost 1 per unit per period carried. Silver-Meal extends each order while the average cost per covered period decreases. By how much does its plan's setup plus holding cost exceed that of the cheapest plan?

Demands are $D=(10,30,10)$, setup costs $K_1=40$, $K_2=20$, $K_3=40$ and holding cost 1 per unit per period carried. Silver-Meal, averaging setup plus holding cost per covered period, orders all 50 units in period 1 at cost 90. Which order plan is cheapest?
